correctness.rationale: The exact cofactor/Jacobian formulas imply \(Z=(u^{\mathsf T}Qu)(u^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}u)\). The spectral endpoint inequality proves the maximum K and its precisely four maximizing normals. At each maximizer the two-variable deficit is \(B s^2+D y^2+O(r^3)\), \(D=(B-A-C)/2>0\); exact spherical Haar area dtheta dy/(4pi) gives slope \(\gamma=1/\sqrt{BD}\), with no unbounded residual region. Algebra then gives k and the roots t,k/t, while \(Q\mapsto Q^{-1}\) keeps Z pointwise unchanged, proving sharp identifiability. Exact fraction computations test nonstandard algebra; independent conditional arcsine integration confirms the upper-tail coefficient on several triples; finite examples are not treated as a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement identifies the complete inverse image of two sharp upper-tail statistics of a correlated same-direction section/projection quotient. The closest inspected geometric literature concerns full direction-labelled sections, separate marginal distributions, reconstruction from section-only moments, or one-spike section radii. Classical Kantorovich bounds establish only the support endpoint, not the slope and two-parameter polar-identifiability theorem. value.rationale: The two numbers K and gamma are genuinely observable features of a single dimensionless paired geometric measurement and recover the complete two-parameter triaxial shape modulo an unavoidable polar symmetry. The sharp cap probability measures scarcity of maximally distorted viewing directions; it is not obtainable from the standard bound K alone because K is independent of the middle axis. The exact inverse and its necessary twofold obstruction solve a natural scale-invariant tomography problem and provide a reproducible benchmark, independent of any large downstream theorem.
